subject: knight
reasoning:
I'm planning a humanoid knight model around 1.85m tall, sketching out a skeleton hierarchy from hips through spine, neck, head, and limbs, with joints defined using at/aim positioning to keep the rig correct and avoid API mistakes.

I'm laying out leg chains with mirrored hip/knee/ankle/toe points for both sides, planning rigid armor pieces as rods or capsules bound to specific bones rather than smooth sweeps, and defining the spine chain from hips upward through chest to neck base to build the core structure.

Now I'm adding explicit joints for the neck, head, and jaw, each parented to the previous with simple aim directions, before moving on to set up the shoulder joints for the arms.

For the arm chain, I'm placing shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand-tip joints in a slight A-pose, parented to the chest spine joint, with three names mapping to a three-point chain so the arm role resolves correctly. Then I'm starting to position pauldron armor geometry at the shoulder.

Adding more armor meshes...

Still shaping tabard geometry and checking it clears the skirt cylinder radius so the gold cross emblem sits visibly in front without clipping.

Adjusting the tabard placement...

I'll simplify and just place the belt as a torus around the hips, scaling it slightly to match the torso's box-ish proportions rather than fuss over exact ellipse math. Moving on to the head now.

For the helmet, I'm building a great helm from a cylinder base with a domed sphere top, adding a separate lower jaw piece with a dark visor slit and breathing slits, plus a red plume curving from the crown down to the back using a bezier sweep.

Still working out helmet proportions...

Now moving to the legs — planning cuisse rods tapering down the thigh, a poleyn sphere with a side wing at the knee, greaves narrowing toward the ankle, and a boxed sabaton with a cone toe for the feet.

For the sword and shield, I'm positioning the kite shield on the left wrist so it faces forward, working out which axes form its thickness versus its face plane, and sketching the kite outline shape.

Now I'm placing the shield slightly in front of the forearm bone, sizing its thickness, and adding a gold boss sphere plus a red field with gold cross emblem as surface decals.

For the sword on the opposite side, I'm deciding between a dynamic held pose versus a classic planted sword with the tip touching the floor—going with the planted look since it's more iconic—and working out the grip position, blade length, and crossguard placement accordingly.

Still writing blade geometry... Also I need to sort out the joint naming convention for limb chains -- figuring out whether a 3-name path (shoulder, elbow, wrist) ends at the wrist as tip, versus needing a 4th name to get a true hand-tip joint.

Working out the sword proportions so the blade, guard, grip, and pommel line up with the hand bone and the blade tip just touches the floor, then starting on a cape mesh extruded behind the figure.

Working out the cape's z-position so the bottom tucks slightly behind the torso, then adding a gradient from red to dark red for its color. I'm also planning a gorget collar cylinder at the neck, a subtle steel mottle paint on the breastplate, and gold trim along the rims for extra detail.

Writing pauldron geometry and part helper signature...

Setting up ground contact for feet and sword tip at y=0, then defining the color palette for steel, gold, red, leather, and cloth undersuit materials. I'm also planning joint hierarchy with hip-parented legs and adding dark rod elements under the armor at joint gaps to hide seams.
